  "one_line_summary": "phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()",
  "vulnerability_summary": "pep_get_sb() calls pskb_may_pull() which may relocate skb head data, then dereferences the stale pointer ph obtained before the pull, causing a slab use-after-free read.",
  "vulnerability_pattern": "Code saves a pointer to skb header data, calls pskb_may_pull() which may reallocate and invalidate that pointer, then dereferences the stale pointer afterward.",
  "patch": "commit 0f71f852a96af9685858ce59fda34ecbf85c283d
Author: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
Date:   Tue Jul 21 01:58:45 2026 -0700

    phonet: pep: fix use-after-free in pep_get_sb()
    
    pep_get_sb() doesn't consider that pskb_may_pull() might have relocated
    the skb data, and continue to access the older pointer, causing UAF.
    
    Reproduced under KASAN:
    
      BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0
      Read of size 1 at addr ff11000105510f50 by task repro/157
       pep_get_sb+0x234/0x3b0
       pipe_handler_do_rcv+0x5f7/0xa10
       pep_do_rcv+0x203/0x410
       __sk_receive_skb+0x471/0x4a0
       phonet_rcv+0x5b3/0x6c0
       __netif_receive_skb+0xcc/0x1d0
    
    Refetch the header with skb_header_pointer() after pskb_may_pull(), so
    the possibly stale pointer is no longer dereferenced. There are better
    ways to solve this, but, this is the less instrusive one.
    
    Fixes: 9641458d3ec4 ("Phonet: Pipe End Point for Phonet Pipes protocol")
    Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
    Signed-off-by: Breno Leitao <leitao@debian.org>
    Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260721-phonet_get_sb_uaf-v1-1-95fd7881cc4e@debian.org
    Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/phonet/pep.c b/net/phonet/pep.c
index 706927139393..31b29e3ca7bc 100644
--- a/net/phonet/pep.c
+++ b/net/phonet/pep.c
@@ -55,6 +55,8 @@ static unsigned char *pep_get_sb(struct sk_buff *skb, u8 *ptype, u8 *plen,
 	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	if (ph == NULL || ph->sb_len < 2 || !pskb_may_pull(skb, ph->sb_len))
 		return NULL;
+	/* pskb_may_pull() may have reallocated the head; refetch ph. */
+	ph = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 2, &h);
 	ph->sb_len -= 2;
 	*ptype = ph->sb_type;
 	*plen = ph->sb_len;
"
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Find candidate RX-path stale-header-pointer-after-pull bugs.

Heuristic: within each function body of net/*.c files that call a
pull/linearize API, find:
  1) a capture of a pointer from skb->data / skb_header_pointer /
     <hdr accessor>(skb) / skb_network_header etc, assigned to a variable
  2) a later pull call (pskb_may_pull / pskb_pull / __pskb_pull_tail /
     skb_linearize / pskb_pull_reserve / pskb_may_pull)
  3) a later dereference of the captured variable (var->field or var[...]
     or *var or var passed as arg to some calls)
where the deref occurs AFTER the pull and there is no re-assignment of the
variable between pull and deref.
"""
import re, os, sys, subprocess

ROOT = "net"
PULL_RE = re.compile(r'\b(pskb_may_pull|pskb_pull|__pskb_pull_tail|skb_linearize|pskb_pull_reserve|skb_linearize)\s*\(')
CAPTURE_RE = re.compile(
    r'^\s*(?:const\s+)?(?:struct\s+)?[\w]+\s*\*+\s*(\w+)\s*=\s*'
    r'(.*(?:skb_header_pointer|skb->data|_hdr\s*\(\s*skb|_header\s*\(\s*skb).*)$')
DEREF_RE = re.compile(r'(\w+)\s*(->|\[)')
IDENT_RE = re.compile(r'\b(\w+)\b')

def func_iter(src):
    """Yield (name, startline_idx, body_lines) using brace matching."""
    lines = src.split('\n')
    funcstart = re.compile(r'^(\w[\w \t\*]*)\(([^;]*)\)\s*\n?\{', re.M)
    for m in funcstart.finditer(src):
        # find opening brace
        bidx = src.find('{', m.start())
        # count braces
        depth = 0
        i = bidx
        while i < len(src):
            if src[i] == '{': depth += 1
            elif src[i] == '}':
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0:
                    break
            i += 1
        body = src[bidx:i+1]
        startline = src[:bidx].count('\n')
        name_m = re.match(r'\w[\w \t\*]*?(\w+)\s*\(', m.group(0))
        name = name_m.group(1) if name_m else '?'
        yield name, startline, body

def line_of(body, idx, offset):
    return offset + body[:idx].count('\n') + 1

def scan_file(path):
    src = open(path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
    out = []
    for fname, off, body in func_iter(src):
        if not PULL_RE.search(body):
            continue
        # collect captures with positions
        captures = []
        for m in re.finditer(r'(?m)^(.*)$', body):
            line = m.group(1)
            cm = CAPTURE_RE.match(line)
            if cm:
                captures.append((cm.group(1), m.start(), line.strip()))
        if not captures:
            continue
        # collect pull calls with positions
        pulls = [(m.start(), m.group(0)) for m in PULL_RE.finditer(body)]
        for var, cpos, cline in captures:
            # strip strings/comments crudely for deref scan
            for ppos, pcall in pulls:
                if ppos <= cpos:
                    continue
                # search for deref after pull, before any reassignment of var
                rest = body[ppos:]
                # find first reassignment of var
                reass = re.search(r'(?m)^\s*(?:.*[^\w&])' + re.escape(var) + r'\s*=[^=]', rest)
                reass_pos = reass.start() if reass else len(rest)
                # find derefs of var in rest before reass
                seg = rest[:reass_pos]
                dm = re.search(r'\b' + re.escape(var) + r'\s*(->|\[)', seg)
                if dm:
                    # skip self-reassignment-like capture
                    dline = off + body[:ppos].count('\n') + rest[:dm.start()].count('\n') + 1
                    out.append((path, fname, var, cline,
                                off + body[:cpos].count('\n') + 1,
                                pcall.split('(')[0], dline,
                                seg[max(0,dm.start()-60):dm.end()+60].replace('\n',' ')))
    return out

results = []
for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(ROOT):
    for f in files:
        if f.endswith('.c'):
            p = os.path.join(dirpath, f)
            try:
                results.extend(scan_file(p))
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"ERR {p}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)

for r in results:
    print(f"{r[0]} :: {r[1]} :: var={r[2]}")
    print(f"   capture L{r[4]}: {r[3][:150]}")
    print(f"   pull: {r[5]} -> stale deref L{r[6]}: ...{r[7]}...")
    print()

Is the caller path an RX path? br_ip6_multicast_query is called from br_ip6_multicast_mld_rcv, from br_multicast_rcv, from br_handle_frame — bridge RX path, i.e. network-received MLD query packets (ICMPv6).
